traits.note: Jepson's Manual of the Flowering Plants of California (1925), read in full, as Aceraceae: flowers regular, polygamous or dioecious; calyx generally 5-cleft; petals as many or none; stamens 3 to 10 on the edge of a disk; pistil 1 with a 2-lobed, 2-celled ovary and 2 styles, ripening a double samara. Jepson eFlora (as quoted in search results; the page itself was not read): stamens 5 to 12; genus summaries say mostly 8.
